# Flygon Flow

> Flygon Flow keeps a MindMap (people, entities and ideas; called charts in the API), a product timeline, a DevOps board and AgentFlow (agents and workflows) in one workspace per environment. People use the web app. Agents use the same operations through the REST API, the MCP server or the CLI, authenticated with a personal API key (`flow_…`).

Releases: `GET /api/devlog` on your Flow server (one per production deploy), also in the app under Settings › DevLog.

# Concepts

## Environments

An **environment** is one workspace: its charts, projects, timeline and DevOps board, plus a record of who owns it.

```json
{"id": "acme-hq", "name": "Acme HQ", "ownerEmail": "owner@example.com", "visibility": "private", "members": []}
```

- Every user starts in a new, empty, private environment. They can create more, rename them and archive them from Settings › Environment. Archiving hides an environment and keeps its data.
- **Isolation.** A private environment can only be seen by its owner and its members. Anyone else gets `404`, so the server does not even confirm that it exists. Anyone signed in can read a public environment, but only its owner can write to it.
- Every API operation that touches workspace data is scoped to one environment through the `{env}` path segment. The server runs the read or write check before it touches any data.
- Data saved before environments existed belongs to the instance's default environment.

## MindMap (charts)

The app's **MindMap** tab is a free-form canvas of **cards** joined by **edges**. The API calls each mind map a **chart** (`charts.list`, `nodes.*`, `edges.*`). A workspace can hold several charts; one of them is active. In the app, right-clicking a card, a connection or empty canvas opens a menu of the actions that apply there.

- Card types: `entity` (a company or organisation), `person`, `area` (a project area that groups cards inside it) and `note`.
- Edge types: `ownership` is a solid arrow that can carry a percentage from 0 to 100, or `""` when the percentage is unknown. `group` is a dashed line that means grouping only.
- Cards snap to a 16px grid and can be resized. Moving an area also moves every card that sits fully inside it.
- A `person` card can have a **photo** (`image`: an `https://` URL, or a `data:image/png|jpeg|webp;base64,` URL of at most 61,440 characters) and an **email** (`email`, up to 200 characters, stored lower-case). In the app, the person's side panel can upload a photo (cropped to a 128px square), remove it, or **Use my photo** to take your account photo and email. A person whose email is yours shows your account photo until they get one of their own; so does a person with no email who is the only person in the workspace with your account name (matched ignoring case and extra spaces). **This is me** (shown when you are signed in and the person has no email) sets their email to yours, so they keep showing your live account photo. Matching only changes what is displayed: nothing is saved until you choose one of these buttons. The photo then appears wherever that person does: their card, DevOps assignee bubbles, pickers and AgentFlow supervisor badges. Invalid values, and photos or emails on other card types, are dropped.
- Sharing a person shares their photo with whoever can see the card, but never their email.
- Selecting an entity or area shows its **project strip**: the projects placed under it, their next timeline item, backlog counts and open DevOps cards.

```json
{"id": "c1", "name": "Acme · structure",
 "nodes": [{"id": "acme", "name": "Acme Holdings", "type": "entity", "x": 400, "y": 0},
           {"id": "rivera", "name": "Sam Rivera", "type": "person", "x": 320, "y": 144}],
 "edges": [{"id": "o1", "from": "rivera", "to": "acme", "type": "ownership", "percent": "60"}]}
```

Validation is strict: ids must be unique, every edge must join two existing cards, and a card cannot connect to itself.

## Timeline

The timeline holds dated **items** that are tagged with **projects**.

- Item kinds: `feature`, `milestone`, `release`, `deadline`, `project`, `phase`, `event`.
- Status: `planned`, `active`, `risk`, `blocked`, `done`, `cancelled`. Priority (`high`, `medium`, `low`) is optional.
- `start` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, or empty for an unscheduled backlog item that appears only on the Board and List views. `end` is optional and never earlier than `start`.
- A feature can target a **release** by title. The release then lists the items that target it and how many of them are done.
- **Projects** are coloured tags `{id, name, color, entity}`. A project can sit under a chart entity or area through `entity`.
- Views: Timeline (Gantt), Calendar, List and Board (a kanban by status). Filtered items can be exported as `.ics`.

## DevOps board and gates

The DevOps board is a card board. Each card has an auto-incrementing `#number`.

Columns, in order: `requests` (Requests / Sprinted, where new cards land), `doing`, `blocked`, `uat`, `done`, then the two backlogs `must` (Must Have) and `nice` (Nice to Have).

A card holds `title, description, column, project, labels[], points, due, assignees[{node, role}], checklist[{text, done}], links[{kind, url}], item` and the `created` / `updated` / `moved` timestamps. Assignee roles are `developer`, `tester` and `requester`, and each assignee is a person card on the chart. Link kinds are `pr`, `commit` and `url`. `item` links the card to a timeline item. Responses also list `agents`, the AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (see AgentFlow: delegation and the work queue).

### Gates

Some moves need a confirmation or a decision. The app asks for it, and API callers must provide it explicitly:

| Move | Gate |
| --- | --- |
| UAT → Done with **Approve** | none (approval is the gate) |
| anything else → `done` | `confirm-done` |
| `done` → anything | `confirm-reopen` (reopen) |
| → `doing` with no developer | `pick-dev`: choose who develops it |

Labels have a section (`priority`, `urgency`, `area`, `topic`, `other`) and a colour key. Due dates turn amber two days before they are due and red once they are overdue.

## Agent inbox

Agents can add or update projects, labels, timeline items and cards by dropping a JSON **patch** into the inbox. The open app picks the patch up within about 20 seconds and merges it as **one undoable step**.

```json
{"source": "Claude", "env": "acme-hq", "ops": [
  {"op": "upsertProject", "name": "Launch", "color": "#7cb980"},
  {"op": "upsertCard", "title": "Write release notes", "project": "Launch", "column": "requests", "labels": ["High"]},
  {"op": "patchCard", "number": 12, "column": "uat"}
]}
```

- Ops: `upsertProject`, `upsertLabel`, `upsertItem`, `upsertCard`, `patchCard`.
- References use names: a project by name, an assignee by the name of a person card, an item or release by title, and a label by id or name.
- **Safety:** ops only add or update and never delete. Lists only grow. A field a human changed after the patch was written is kept, and the merge notes it. Applying the same patch again changes nothing.
- CLI: `node tools/inbox.mjs add|check|list|requeue`.

The token API is the direct way to make changes. The inbox suits agents that cannot hold a token, or changes a human should be able to undo in one click.

## Sync

The server is the source of truth. Each environment's workspace is stored with a **revision** number, and the browser keeps an offline cache.

- `GET /api/workspace?env=<id>` returns `{rev, data}`. `PUT` with `{baseRev, data}` saves the workspace when `baseRev` is still current.
- If the workspace has moved on, the save gets `409` along with the newer copy. The client then merges per entity and field and retries. When both sides changed the same field, the local change wins. A deletion only applies to an entity the other side has not touched.
- A save that would drop most of a large workspace is refused with `422`, unless it is a deliberate load or replace.
- AgentFlow runners belong to the server: only `runners.report` changes them. A `PUT` keeps the runners as they last reported (their models and scheduled jobs), even when the saved copy is missing them or holds an older report, such as a tab still running an older version of Flow. The answer then includes `runnersKept: true`, and the client reads the workspace again.
- Every write first keeps the previous revision in the history. Postgres keeps it in `flygon_flow_workspace_history`; without Postgres it goes to `BACKUP_DIR/workspaces/history/`.
- Open tabs pick up remote changes every 20 seconds, and offline edits upload when the connection comes back.

API writes go through the same revision check, so an agent's change and a human's edit never silently overwrite each other.

## Sharing

The owner of an environment can share part of it with another Flow user, by email: a person and everything below them, hand-picked cards, a project, a DevOps label, or the whole environment. The Share dialog (a card's **Share…** button, or Settings › Environment › *Share this environment…*) shows a live preview of exactly what the other person will see. Permissions are **view**, **comment** or **edit**.

The recipient finds it under Settings › Sharing › *Shared with you* and adds it to one of their own environments. The shared cards appear there as linked boxes with their own layout. Direct co-owners of a shared card show as read-only name stubs, and nothing else of theirs is shared. Edits travel both ways as the permission allows. Revoking a share removes everything from the recipient's environment. Recipients cannot share further; instead they ask the owner, who approves or denies the request.

The server enforces all of this: linked copies are computed from the owner's data on every read and are never stored in the recipient's environment. The API, the CLI and MCP see each environment's own data only. Details: `docs/sharing.md`.

The owner can also invite people to the app itself (Settings › Account › *Invite to Flow*). The invited person signs in with that email and gets their own empty environment.

## Versioning

Flygon Flow uses [Bradshaw Versioning](https://github.com/aribradshaw/devlog/blob/main/docs/bradshaw-versioning.md) numbers. Every production deploy gets the next `YEAR.MONTH.UPDATE`:

- The year is zero-based from 2026, so October 2026 is `0.10.x` and January 2027 is `1.1.x`. Months are calendar months, in the America/Phoenix timezone.
- One release per deploy. A release lists every commit the deploy brought, plus `compatibility` (`compatible`, `action-required` or `breaking`, with the required `action`).
- The server records the release when the deploy starts. Nothing is committed back to the repository.
- `public/devlog.json` is the frozen history from before deploy releases (up to `0.11.25`).

The app's Settings › DevLog and `GET /api/devlog` list every release, newest first.

## AgentFlow

AgentFlow is an org chart for agentic work. You lay out the agents that do work for a business, say what each one is for and what it takes in and produces, chain them into workflows, and tie them to the projects, DevOps cards and deadlines they own.

Flow stores the design. It does not run agents itself. A runner of your choice (an agent harness, a home server, a cron job) reads an agent's or workflow's **brief** through the API or MCP and does the work, then reports back on the DevOps cards like anyone else.

### Agents

An agent has `name, kind, title, status, live, reportsTo, supervisor, purpose, instructions, runtime, models[], model, auto, schedule, inputs[], outputs[], tools[]`, an optional `job`, and links `projects[], cards[], items[]`.

- `kind`: `agent` (an AI agent), `human`, `team` (a group heading in the org) or `automation` (a scripted job without AI, such as a backup timer, that runs on its own schedule outside Flow; see [Automations](#automations)).
- `schedule` says when it runs, in plain words or cron, such as "Weekdays 09:00" or `30 22 * * *` (`""` for none). For an AI agent it is a note carried in the brief: the reference runner works by Live and its queue, and does not start work from it.
- `job` is `{runner, id}`: the runner job it was promoted from (see [Scheduled jobs](#scheduled-jobs)). It is absent when there is none; send `null` or `""` to `agents.update` to clear it.
- `status`: `draft`, `active`, `paused` or `retired`.
- `reportsTo` is another agent. Together these form the AgentFlow org chart. An agent cannot report to itself or to anyone below it (`reports_loop`). A saved loop is broken when the workspace loads.
- `supervisor` is a person card on one of your mind maps: the human accountable for the agent. A `human` agent shows a person's photo: its supervisor's, else that of the only person card with the agent's name, else your account photo when the agent has your account name and no person card does.
- `inputs`, `outputs` and `tools` are short text lists, such as "A card in Doing" or "Pull request linked on the card".
- `instructions` holds the system prompt or runbook. `runtime` says where it runs (a runner's name).
- `models` lists the models it may run on, up to 10 ids from its runner, in order: the **primary** first, then **fallbacks** the runner tries when one fails (a rate or usage limit, a provider that is down). `model` is always the first of them, kept for older runners; sending `model` alone to `agents.update` sets `models` to just it, and when both are sent `models` wins.
- `auto` turns `models` into a pool: the runner picks one per card instead of always starting on the first. The org card shows **Auto (N models)**, or the primary model and **+N** for its fallbacks.
- `live` is the switch runners obey. It is off for every new agent, and a runner leaves an agent that is not live alone, whatever its status. Turn it on in the agent's side panel, or with `agents.update` (`live: true`). The org card then shows a **Live** badge, in amber when its runner would skip it (no runner or model picked, or a model its runner did not report).
- Deleting an agent moves its direct reports up to its manager, and its workflow steps become unassigned.

### Runners

A runner is a machine or service that runs agents, such as a home server with agent harnesses installed. It tells Flow what it can run with `runners.report`: its name and the models it offers, each with an id, a label and optionally a `provider` to group it under (such as "Claude" or "OpenCode") and `billing`: `included` (covered by a subscription, or free) or `metered` (paid per use). `runners.list` returns them. In an agent's side panel, **Runs on** suggests the reported runners and **Models** that runner's models, and every org card shows where the agent runs and on which model. Reporting the same models again saves nothing, so a runner can report on every pass.

```sh
flow runners report --input '{"runner":"Home server","models":[{"id":"claudeAgent:claude-sonnet-5-5","label":"Claude · Sonnet 5.5","provider":"Claude","billing":"included"}]}'
```

`tools/agent-runner.mjs` is a reference runner for [T3 Code](https://t3.codes): it reports the providers and models signed in on its machine, and for each live agent whose `runtime` is its name, starts a T3 thread on the agent's model for the top card in its queue, then moves the card to UAT when the thread finishes. If a model will not start, or its thread fails or hits a limit, it starts the card again on the next model and keeps every attempt; when all have failed it leaves the card and logs it. For an `auto` agent it prefers `included` models over `metered` ones, keeping the pool's order, and can ask a small "router" model to choose among the included ones from the card and the agent's purpose. It marks Claude, Codex, Cursor, Grok and Antigravity models `included`, OpenCode's own free models (`opencode/…`) `included` and other OpenCode models `metered`, and its settings can override that. It starts in dry-run mode, so it only prints what it would do until you turn that off. See the comment at the top of the file for its settings.

### Scheduled jobs

A runner can also tell Flow which scheduled jobs it found: systemd timers, crontab lines, scheduled T3, Claude or Aside tasks, Codex automations, Vercel or Railway crons, GitHub Actions schedules, Windows scheduled tasks. It sends them as `jobs` in the same `runners.report` call, up to 500 per runner:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `id` | Required, up to 200 characters, stable per runner, e.g. `systemd:backup.timer` or `vercel:my-app:/api/cron/sync`. |
| `name` | Up to 120 characters (defaults to the id). |
| `source` | Where it is scheduled, up to 40 characters: `systemd`, `cron`, `t3`, `vercel`, `railway`, `aside`, `windows`, `claude`, `codex`, `github` or `other` (the default). Other text is kept as it is. |
| `group` | A display group, up to 120 characters, e.g. "Home server" or "Vercel · my-app". |
| `schedule` | When, in words, up to 200 characters: "Daily 22:30", "Every 5 min". |
| `cron` | The cron expression, when there is one (up to 120). |
| `timezone` | The zone its times are in, up to 64 characters: an IANA name such as `America/Phoenix`, `UTC`, or `local` (the runner's own zone; see below). |
| `triggers` | Every rule it fires on, up to 10: `{kind, expr, text}`. `kind` is `cron`, `calendar` (a calendar rule such as a systemd `OnCalendar` line or a daily or weekly Windows trigger), `interval`, `logon`, `boot`, `once`, `rrule` (RFC 5545), `manual` or `other`; `expr` is the raw expression as the scheduler holds it (up to 200), such as `*/5 * * * *`, `Mon *-*-* 09:00:00` or `OnUnitActiveSec=5min`; `text` is it in words (up to 200). |
| `origin` | Where the schedule was read: `repo` (a config file in a repo), `platform` (the hosting platform's API) or `machine` (the machine's own scheduler). |
| `file` | The repo-relative path of the config it came from (up to 200), such as `services/worker/railway.json`. |
| `drift` | How the platform's live schedule differs from the repo file, when it does (up to 200). |
| `note` | Conditions the job's script applies itself, such as "Exits early when nothing changed" (up to 500). |
| `command` | A short summary of what it runs (up to 300). |
| `ai` | `true` when the job starts an AI agent. |
| `enabled` | `false` when it is switched off on the runner (default `true`). |
| `lastRun`, `nextRun` | ISO times. |
| `lastStatus` | `ok`, `failed`, `running` or `unknown` (the default). |

The report can also say the runner machine's `timezone` (an IANA name), which jobs with `timezone: "local"` are in; left out, the stored one stays. `jobs` replaces the stored list. Leave it out to keep the stored jobs, or send `[]` to clear them. `models` is optional too: leave it out to keep the stored models, as a runner does when it reports the jobs of another machine it reaches over SSH. To keep writes down, a report is not saved when the only changes are `lastRun` and `nextRun`, unless the jobs were last saved six hours ago or more. A changed `lastStatus`, a job added or removed, or any other field (a new trigger, drift or note) always saves. The runner's `jobsReported` is when its jobs were last saved, and the response's `changed` says whether this report was.

```sh
flow runners report --input '{"runner":"Home server","models":[],"timezone":"America/Phoenix","jobs":[{"id":"systemd:backup.timer","name":"Nightly backup","source":"systemd","group":"Home server","schedule":"Daily 22:30","timezone":"America/Phoenix","triggers":[{"kind":"calendar","expr":"*-*-* 22:30:00","text":"Daily 22:30"}],"origin":"machine","command":"restic backup /srv","lastStatus":"ok","lastRun":"2026-11-02T05:30:00Z","nextRun":"2026-11-03T05:30:00Z"}]}'
```

In the app, **Scheduled** in the org chart's toolbar opens a tray on the left of the canvas. It lists every runner's jobs by runner and group, each with its source icon, name, schedule and a dot for the last run (green OK, red failed, grey unknown). Hover the dot for the last and next run. A row names the time zone (such as `UTC`) only when it is not yours and the schedule has a time of day, and shows an amber dot when the schedule has drifted from its repo file. Click a row, or its **i**, for the job's details: the schedule in words, every trigger with its raw expression, the time zone (always named; a `local` job shows its runner's zone), where it was read (**Repo file** with the file's path, **Platform** or **Machine**), drift in amber, the note, the command, the last run and its status, the next run (when, in your time and the job's zone), whether it starts an AI agent and whether it is enabled. **Promote to org** is there too. Escape or a click elsewhere closes it. A group with more than eight jobs starts collapsed to a chip such as "59 jobs" that opens it. Search filters the tray too. Whether the tray is open, and which groups you opened or closed, is remembered on this device.

The reference runner (`tools/agent-runner.mjs`) reports the jobs it finds with every `report` and `tick`: systemd user and system timers (stock distribution timers such as apt-daily, fstrim and logrotate are skipped), the user's crontab, T3 scheduled tasks (read only from T3's database; needs Node 22.5+ for `node:sqlite`), and cron configs in your repos: `vercel.json` crons, `cronSchedule` in `railway.json`/`railway.toml`, and `on.schedule` in GitHub Actions workflows. Repos default to your T3 projects' folders. Commands are summarised on one line with anything that looks like a secret hidden. Every job comes with its full schedule: its `timezone` (this machine's zone, from `timedatectl` or Node; the zone an `OnCalendar` line names; a crontab's `CRON_TZ`; UTC for repo crons), its `triggers` (each `OnCalendar` line as a calendar trigger, `OnUnitActiveSec` as an interval and `OnBootSec` as boot; each crontab line; T3's schedule as T3 holds it), its `origin`, and for repo crons the `file`. Run `node tools/agent-runner.mjs jobs` (or `jobs --json`, with every field) to see the list without contacting Flow; the table has **TZ** and **ORIGIN** columns, and `!` after the origin marks drift. Tune it with `"jobs"` in `runner.json`: `sources`, `repos`, `exclude`, `include` (keeps a job even when `skipDistro` or `exclude` would drop it), `skipDistro` and `notes`; `"jobs": false` stops reporting jobs and leaves the stored list as it is.

**Notes.** For a Railway cron, the runner reads the README in the service's folder (else its start command's script, and for a Vercel cron its route's source) and takes the first sentence that says it runs every N minutes, exits, or applies a condition ("only when", "unless", "unchanged", "skips", "does not run"), plus the first condition after it when both fit in 200 characters. It never uses a sentence that mentions a token, secret, password or credential, and hides anything that looks like one. `"notes": {"<job id or name>": "text"}` in `"jobs"` (globs or substrings, first match) wins; `""` removes a note.

**Platform schedules.** A repo file says what should run; the platform says what does. With a token, the runner reads the live cron schedules and matches them to the repo's cron configs:

- `railwayToken` (or `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN`): every service's cron schedule and next run from Railway's GraphQL API, matched to `railway.json` configs by service name (`railwayWorkspace` picks a workspace's projects).
- `vercelToken` (or `VERCEL_TOKEN`): each project's crons from Vercel's API, matched to `vercel.json` by the folder's `.vercel/project.json` link, else by project name (`vercelTeam`, a team id or slug, for team projects).

A matched job is reported as the platform runs it (origin `platform`, with its `file` kept) and its next run from the platform, and `drift` says how the file differs, such as "Railway runs `*/10 * * * *` (Every 10 min); services/worker/railway.json has `*/5 * * * *` (Every 5 min)", or that the platform has no cron for it. A live cron that no repo file has is reported too. Without a token nothing is asked; `"platform": false` in `"jobs"` turns it off. Put tokens only in your own `runner.json` (or the environment), never in a repo.

#### Remote machines

The reference runner can also read the scheduled jobs of other machines over SSH, such as a Windows laptop, and report each one as a runner of its own, named after it. It sends that runner's `jobs` only, so the remote shows in the Scheduled tray (and its jobs can be promoted) without any models. List them as `"remotes"` in `runner.json`:

```json
"remotes": [{"name": "Laptop", "ssh": ["ssh", "-i", "~/.ssh/laptop_key", "-o", "BatchMode=yes", "me@laptop"],
             "python": "C:\\Python\\python.exe", "timezone": "America/Phoenix"}]
```

- `ssh` is the ssh command as a list, ending with the host. Use a key and `BatchMode=yes` so it never asks for a password. The remote's login shell may be `cmd.exe`: the runner sends its scripts on stdin, PowerShell through `powershell -EncodedCommand`, and Python when `python` (the path to `python.exe` on the remote) is set. Both scripts only read.
- `timezone` is the remote's time zone (an IANA name). Its cron lines and schedules are read in that zone, and its jobs and runner report it. It defaults to the runner's own.
- `sources` picks what to read (all by default):
  - `windows`: Task Scheduler tasks outside `\Microsoft\`, with their triggers in words ("Daily 18:00", "Every 15 min", "At logon", "On demand") and each trigger's raw settings (its type, start, days and repetition, such as `TimeTrigger, start 2026-10-15T08:51:32-07:00, repeat PT15M`), last and next run, and status from the last result. Vendor updater tasks (Adobe, Edge, Google, Zoom, McAfee, HP, OneDrive and so on) are skipped unless `skipVendor` is `false` or `include` names them.
  - `aside`: Aside routines, active and paused (`keepDone` adds completed ones). Each shows its schedule from its RRULE (one-shots as "Once Nov 1 18:00"; the raw rule and its TZID are its trigger and zone), its model and prompt, and its last run. A routine waiting for approval shows as running, with "Waiting for approval". One whose next run has already passed is marked "(stale)". Needs `python`: Aside's database is copied to a temporary folder, read and removed.
  - `claude-desktop`: Claude desktop scheduled tasks, with what each one does taken from its `SKILL.md`.
  - `codex`: Codex automations, from their RRULE or cron line and status. One-shots whose runs are used up are skipped (`keepDone` keeps them, marked "(done)"). With `python`, the last run of each cron automation comes from Codex's database.
  - `vercel`, `railway`, `github`: cron configs in the repos listed in `repos` (paths on the remote).
- `include`, `exclude` and `notes` work as in `"jobs"`. `timeout` is in seconds for the whole remote (40 by default), and `enabled: false` turns a remote off.

`tick` reads the remotes after its own pass, at most every 15 minutes, and keeps the time in its state file. `report` reads them every time. A remote that cannot be reached is logged and tried again next time, after one retry if the connection fails, and it never holds up the local pass. Run `node tools/agent-runner.mjs jobs --remote Laptop` to see a remote's jobs without contacting Flow, or `jobs --all` for this machine and every remote.

#### Promoting a job

To put a job in the org, do one of these:

- Drag the job onto an agent's card. It becomes that agent's report.
- Drag it onto empty canvas to place it at the top level, right there.
- Click **Promote** on the row (top level).
- Right-click it and choose **Promote to org**, or **Promote under** the selected agent.

The new agent is selected and its side panel opens. Undo removes it again. A job without AI becomes an **automation**, and an `ai` job becomes an AI agent whose `runtime` is the runner (pick its models, then switch it to Live). Either way the agent is named after the job, its role comes from the source (such as "Vercel cron" or "systemd timer"), its `schedule` is the job's (or its cron line), its purpose is the command, and its status is Active, or Paused when the job is disabled. It is never live, and `job` links it back. A job is promoted once: its row then shows **Promoted** (click it to select the agent), and promoting it again selects the agent it already became.

### Automations

An automation (`kind: "automation"`) is a scripted job in the org with no AI in it. It runs on its own schedule, outside Flow, so it has no runner, no models and no Live switch: `live` is always false, and a runner never works it. Its card is shorter and grey, with a gear, and shows its schedule (and its job's last status) where an AI agent's card shows its runner and model. Its side panel has a **Schedule** section with the schedule, and, when it came from a runner job, the same details as the Scheduled tray shows for it under **Promoted from**: triggers with their raw expressions, time zone, origin and file, drift, note, command, last and next run (read-only, as the runner reports them). An AI agent's `schedule` is under **Runs on**, and its card shows a small clock when it has one.

The brief lists `Schedule: …` and `Promoted from: <runner> · <job name>` under Runtime.

### Workflows

A workflow has `name, description, status, trigger, schedule, steps[{agent, action, output}]` and the same links. `trigger` is `manual`, `schedule` or `event`. `schedule` says when or on what in plain words, e.g. "Weekdays at 09:00" or "A card enters UAT". Steps run in order, and each one names the agent that handles it.

### Delegation and the work queue

Delegating a DevOps card to an agent puts it in that agent's **work queue**. The person on the card stays accountable; the agent does the work. Delegate in the card's **Delegated to** picker, from the agent's side panel (Cards), or with `cards.update` (`agents: ["Researcher"]`; `[]` clears it). Cards show their agents as square badges, and the board's **Agents** filter shows one agent's cards. A card can be delegated to several agents.

`agents.work` returns everything a runner needs in one call: the agent, its brief, and its queue, which holds the open delegated cards. The queue is ordered Doing, Requests / Sprinted, Blocked, UAT, then the backlogs, and by soonest due date and `#number` within each. `columns: ["doing","requests"]` keeps only the cards it can act on now. A runner loop on any machine looks like this:

1. `agents.work` with the agent's name and `columns: ["doing","requests"]`.
2. Take the first card. Move it to Doing with `cards.move` if it is new.
3. Do the work, following the brief and the card's description and checklist.
4. Report back with `cards.update` (tick the checklist, add the pull request under `links`), then `cards.move` to `uat` for a human to approve.

A runner only works agents with `live` on: `agents.list` with `live: true` gives it that list.

```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_TOKEN" "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/$FLOW_ENV/agents/Researcher/work?columns=doing,requests"
flow agents work --input '{"agent":"Researcher","columns":["doing","requests"]}'   # or the agents_work MCP tool
```

The runner only calls out to Flow and never needs to be reachable itself, so it works from a home server behind a router.

### Briefs

`agents.get` and `workflows.get` return a `brief`: Markdown with everything a runner needs. That covers purpose, reporting line, inputs, outputs, tools, runtime, workflow steps, linked projects, cards (open ones from linked projects too) and deadlines, and the instructions. In the app, **Copy brief** in the side panel puts the same text on the clipboard.

### In the app

The AgentFlow tab has two views: **Org chart** (`1`) and **Workflows** (`2`). **Scheduled** opens the tray of runner jobs (see [Scheduled jobs](#scheduled-jobs)). The org chart is a canvas like the MindMap: drag empty space to pan, scroll to zoom, drag a card to move it (Shift: with its reports), and drag the dot under a card onto another agent to make that agent report to it, or onto empty space to add a new report. Each AI agent's card shows small icons for the makers of its models in the bottom-right corner (the primary first, then up to two fallbacks and "+N"), or one auto symbol with a count when it is on Auto, and its supervisor's face sits on the corner of its avatar. Double-click empty space to add an agent. **Tidy up** returns to the automatic tree. In the tree, a manager's reports that have no reports of their own are stacked in indented columns (up to six per column) once there are three or more, so a large team stays compact and no reporting lines cross. Positions are saved as the agent's optional `x` and `y`. An agent without them, such as one added through the API, is placed under its manager, below the last of its teammates. `N` adds an agent under the selected one, `W` adds a workflow, `/` searches, `F` fits the org, arrow keys nudge the selected agent. Right-click (or the menu key) opens a menu on an agent, a reporting line, a workflow card or empty canvas: change kind, status or manager, add the agent to a workflow, open its work queue on the DevOps board, duplicate a workflow, and so on. **Start from a template** creates a small example org and workflow to edit. A DevOps card's detail shows the agents linked to it, and you can assign agents from there.

# Using the API

Every operation is an HTTP call under the base URL of your Flow server:

```sh
curl -sS "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/$FLOW_ENV/cards" -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

Keys look like `flow_…` and carry a scope: `read` (list and get), `write` (create, update and move) or `admin` (keys, sharing and environments). The OpenAPI document is at `/api/v1/openapi.json`. Errors come back with an HTTP status plus a `code` and a `message`. Path parameters such as `{env}` are filled from the input. Any other input is sent as the query string for GET and DELETE, or as the JSON body otherwise.

## Environments

### `envs.list`

List environments

`GET /api/v1/envs` · scope `read` · MCP tool `envs_list`

Environments (workspaces) you own, newest first. Use an id from here as {env} in every other call.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].visibility` | enum | yes | One of `private`, `public`. |
| `items[].owner` | string |  |  |
| `items[].rev` | integer | yes |  |
| `items[].updatedAt` | string | null |  |  |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |

**Example: Your environments**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "default-workspace",
      "name": "Default workspace",
      "visibility": "private",
      "owner": "owner@example.test",
      "rev": 42,
      "updatedAt": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null
}
```

### `envs.get`

Get an environment

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}` · scope `read` · MCP tool `envs_get`

One environment: name, visibility, owner, revision and how much it holds.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `environment` | object | yes |  |
| `environment.id` | string | yes |  |
| `environment.name` | string | yes |  |
| `environment.visibility` | enum | yes | One of `private`, `public`. |
| `environment.owner` | string |  |  |
| `environment.rev` | integer | yes |  |
| `environment.updatedAt` | string | null |  |  |
| `environment.counts` | object |  |  |

**Example: Default workspace**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "environment": {
    "id": "default-workspace",
    "name": "Default workspace",
    "visibility": "private",
    "owner": "owner@example.test",
    "rev": 42,
    "updatedAt": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "counts": {
      "charts": 1,
      "nodes": 7,
      "edges": 7,
      "projects": 3,
      "items": 12,
      "cards": 40
    }
  }
}
```

## Nodes

### `nodes.list`

List nodes

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/charts/{chart}/nodes` · scope `read` · MCP tool `nodes_list`

Cards on a chart (entities, people, areas, notes). Filter by `type`, or by `q` (name contains).

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `chart` | string | yes | Chart id, or "active" for the chart open in the app. |
| `type` | enum |  | One of `entity`, `person`, `area`, `note`. |
| `q` | string |  |  |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].type` | enum | yes | One of `entity`, `person`, `area`, `note`. |
| `items[].x` | number | yes |  |
| `items[].y` | number | yes |  |
| `items[].w` | number |  |  |
| `items[].h` | number |  |  |
| `items[].notes` | string |  |  |
| `items[].image` | string |  | Person photo: an https URL or a data:image/(png\|jpeg\|webp);base64 URL. |
| `items[].email` | string |  | Person email, matching them to an account. |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |

**Example: People on the active chart**

```sh

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json

  "items": [

      "id": "cleo",
      "name": "Cleo Park",
      "type": "person",
      "x": 320,
      "y": 144,
      "notes": ""
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null,
  "rev": 42
```
```json
}
```

### `nodes.create`

Create a node

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/charts/{chart}/nodes` · scope `write` · MCP tool `nodes_create`

Add a card to a chart. Without x/y it is placed at the origin, stepping 32px diagonally past occupied spots (as the app does).

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `chart` | string | yes | Chart id, or "active" for the chart open in the app. |
| `type` | enum | yes | One of `entity`, `person`, `area`, `note`. |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `notes` | string |  |  |
| `w` | number |  |  |
| `h` | number |  |  |
| `image` | string |  | Person cards only: a photo as an https URL, or a data:image/(png\|jpeg\|webp);base64 URL up to 61440 characters. "" removes it. |
| `email` | string |  | Person cards only: their email, so the app can show the matching account photo. Never shared with share recipients. "" removes it. |
| `x` | number |  |  |
| `y` | number |  |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `node` | object | yes |  |
| `node.id` | string | yes |  |
| `node.name` | string | yes |  |
| `node.type` | enum | yes | One of `entity`, `person`, `area`, `note`. |
| `node.x` | number | yes |  |
| `node.y` | number | yes |  |
| `node.w` | number |  |  |
| `node.h` | number |  |  |
| `node.notes` | string |  |  |
| `node.image` | string |  | Person photo: an https URL or a data:image/(png\|jpeg\|webp);base64 URL. |
| `node.email` | string |  | Person email, matching them to an account. |

**Example: Add a person**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/charts/active/nodes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"type":"person","name":"Cleo Park","x":320,"y":144}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 43,
  "node": {
    "id": "cleo",
    "name": "Cleo Park",
    "type": "person",
    "x": 320,
    "y": 144,
    "notes": ""
  }
}
```

| `h` | number |  |  |
| `image` | string |  | Person cards only: a photo as an https URL, or a data:image/(png\|jpeg\|webp);base64 URL up to 61440 characters. "" removes it. |
| `email` | string |  | Person cards only: their email, so the app can show the matching account photo. Never shared with share recipients. "" removes it. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `node.h` | number |  |  |
| `node.notes` | string |  |  |

**Example: Rename**

```sh
curl -sS -X PATCH "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/charts/active/nodes/flygon" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Kestrel Group"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 43,
  "node": {
    "id": "flygon",
    "name": "Kestrel Group",
    "type": "entity",
    "x": 400,
    "y": 0,
    "notes": ""
  }
```


### `edges.create`

Create an edge

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/charts/{chart}/edges` · scope `write` · MCP tool `edges_create`

Connect two cards on the same chart. A second edge between the same pair (same direction) is refused with 409.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `chart` | string | yes | Chart id, or "active" for the chart open in the app. |
| `from` | string | yes | Node id. |
| `to` | string | yes | Node id. |
| `type` | enum |  | One of `ownership`, `group`. |
| `percent` | string | number |  | 0-100, or "" for unspecified. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `edge` | object | yes |  |
| `edge.id` | string | yes |  |
| `edge.from` | string | yes |  |
| `edge.to` | string | yes |  |
| `edge.type` | enum | yes | One of `ownership`, `group`. |
| `edge.percent` | string | yes |  |

**Example: 50% ownership**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/charts/active/edges" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"from":"cleo","to":"quill","percent":"50"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 45,
  "edge": {
    "id": "o1",
    "from": "cleo",
    "to": "quill",
    "type": "ownership",
    "percent": "50"
  }
}
```

### `edges.delete`

Delete an edge

`DELETE /api/v1/envs/{env}/charts/{chart}/edges/{edge}` · scope `write` · MCP tool `edges_delete`

Remove one connection. The cards it joined stay. Earlier revisions are kept in the workspace history.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `chart` | string | yes | Chart id, or "active" for the chart open in the app. |
| `edge` | string | yes | Edge id. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `deleted` | string | yes |  |

**Example: Delete**

```sh
curl -sS -X DELETE "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/charts/active/edges/o1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "rev": 46,
  "deleted": "o1"
}
```

### `projects.create`

Create a project

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/projects` · scope `write` · MCP tool `projects_create`

Add a project. Names are unique (case-insensitive); a duplicate gets 409. Without a colour the next palette colour is used.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `color` | string |  | Hex colour, e.g. #7cb980. |
| `entity` | string |  | The chart entity or area it sits under: node id or name; "" for none. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `project` | object | yes |  |
| `project.id` | string | yes |  |
| `project.name` | string | yes |  |
| `project.color` | string | yes |  |
| `project.entity` | string | yes |  |

**Example: Under Kestrel Group**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/projects" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Lantern","color":"#7cb980","entity":"Kestrel Group"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 47,
  "project": {
    "id": "p1",
    "name": "Lantern",
    "color": "#7cb980",
    "entity": "flygon"
  }
}
```

### `projects.update`

Update a project

`PATCH /api/v1/envs/{env}/projects/{project}` · scope `write` · MCP tool `projects_update`

Rename, recolour or re-parent a project. {project} is its id or name.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `project` | string | yes | Project id or name. |
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `color` | string |  | Hex colour, e.g. #7cb980. |
| `entity` | string |  | The chart entity or area it sits under: node id or name; "" for none. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `project` | object | yes |  |
| `project.id` | string | yes |  |
| `project.name` | string | yes |  |
| `project.color` | string | yes |  |
| `project.entity` | string | yes |  |

**Example: Recolour**

```sh
curl -sS -X PATCH "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/projects/Lantern" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"color":"#3d6fb6"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 48,
  "project": {
    "id": "p1",
    "name": "Lantern",
    "color": "#3d6fb6",
    "entity": "flygon"
  }
}
```

## Timeline

### `items.list`

List timeline items

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/items` · scope `read` · MCP tool `items_list`

Timeline items (milestones, releases, features...). Filter by project (id or name), kind, status or `q` (title contains). Items with start "" are backlog.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `project` | string |  | Project id or name. |
| `kind` | enum |  | One of `feature`, `milestone`, `release`, `deadline`, `project`, `phase`, `event`. |
| `status` | enum |  | One of `planned`, `active`, `risk`, `blocked`, `done`, `cancelled`. |
| `q` | string |  |  |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].title` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].kind` | enum | yes | One of `feature`, `milestone`, `release`, `deadline`, `project`, `phase`, `event`. |
| `items[].status` | enum | yes | One of `planned`, `active`, `risk`, `blocked`, `done`, `cancelled`. |
| `items[].start` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].end` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].priority` | string |  |  |
| `items[].release` | string |  |  |
| `items[].projects` | string[] | yes |  |
| `items[].owner` | string |  |  |
| `items[].link` | string |  |  |
| `items[].notes` | string |  |  |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |

**Example: Releases**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/items?kind=release" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "i1",
      "title": "Public beta",
      "kind": "release",
      "status": "planned",
      "start": "2026-12-01",
      "end": "",
      "priority": "",
      "release": "",
      "projects": [
        "p1"
      ],
      "owner": "",
      "link": "",
      "notes": ""
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null,
  "rev": 42
}
```

| `item.priority` | string |  |  |

```json
    "end": "",

    "owner": "",
    "link": "",
    "notes": ""
```

### `items.create`

Create a timeline item

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/items` · scope `write` · MCP tool `items_create`

Add a timeline item. Without a start date it is backlog (Board and List only). Kind defaults to milestone when dated, feature otherwise.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `title` | string | yes |  |
| `kind` | enum |  | One of `feature`, `milestone`, `release`, `deadline`, `project`, `phase`, `event`. |
| `status` | enum |  | One of `planned`, `active`, `risk`, `blocked`, `done`, `cancelled`. |
| `start` | string |  | YYYY-MM-DD, or "" for none. |
| `end` | string |  | YYYY-MM-DD, or "" for none. |
| `priority` | enum |  | One of `high`, `medium`, `low`, ``. |
| `release` | string |  | A release item: id or title; "" for none. |
| `projects` | string[] |  |  |
| `owner` | string |  |  |
| `link` | string |  |  |
| `notes` | string |  |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `item` | object | yes |  |
| `item.id` | string | yes |  |
| `item.title` | string | yes |  |
| `item.kind` | enum | yes | One of `feature`, `milestone`, `release`, `deadline`, `project`, `phase`, `event`. |
| `item.status` | enum | yes | One of `planned`, `active`, `risk`, `blocked`, `done`, `cancelled`. |
| `item.start` | string | yes |  |
| `item.end` | string | yes |  |
| `item.priority` | string |  |  |
| `item.release` | string |  |  |
| `item.projects` | string[] | yes |  |
| `item.owner` | string |  |  |
| `item.link` | string |  |  |
| `item.notes` | string |  |  |

**Example: A release**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/items" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Public beta","kind":"release","start":"2026-12-01","projects":["Lantern"]}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 49,
  "item": {
    "id": "i1",
    "title": "Public beta",
    "kind": "release",
    "status": "planned",
    "start": "2026-12-01",
    "end": "",
    "priority": "",
    "release": "",
    "projects": [
      "p1"
    ],
    "owner": "",
    "link": "",
    "notes": ""
  }
}
```

**Output**

## DevOps cards

### `cards.list`

List DevOps cards

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/cards` · scope `read` · MCP tool `cards_list`

Board cards in board order. Filters: column, project (id, name or "none"), label (id or name), assignee (person id or name), agent (AgentFlow agent: cards delegated to it), q ("#12" or title text), hideDone.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `column` | string |  | Board column: requests (Requests / Sprinted), doing (Doing), blocked (Blocked), uat (UAT), done (Done), must (Backlog: Must Have), nice (Backlog: Nice to Have). One of `requests`, `doing`, `blocked`, `uat`, `done`, `must`, `nice`. |
| `project` | string |  | Project id or name, or "none". |
| `label` | string |  | Label id or name. |
| `assignee` | string |  | Person node id or name. |
| `agent` | string |  | AgentFlow agent id or name: cards delegated to it. |
| `q` | string |  |  |
| `hideDone` | boolean |  |  |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].number` | integer | yes |  |
| `items[].title` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].description` | string |  |  |
| `items[].column` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].project` | string |  |  |
| `items[].labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `items[].points` | number | null |  |  |
| `items[].due` | string |  |  |
| `items[].assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].item` | string |  |  |
| `items[].created` | string |  |  |
| `items[].updated` | string |  |  |
| `items[].moved` | string |  |  |
| `items[].agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |

**Example: Open cards for a project**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/cards?project=Lantern&hideDone=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "k1",
      "number": 12,
      "title": "Build sign-up form",
      "description": "",
      "column": "requests",
      "project": "p1",
      "labels": [
        "l-high"
      ],
      "points": 3,
      "due": "2026-11-15",
      "assignees": [
        {
          "node": "cleo",
          "role": "developer"
        }
      ],
      "checklist": [
        {
          "id": "x1",
          "text": "Email field",
          "done": false
        }
      ],
      "links": [],
      "item": "i1",
      "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
      "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
      "moved": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
      "agents": [
        "a1"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null,
  "rev": 42
}
```

### `cards.create`

Create a DevOps card

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/cards` · scope `write` · MCP tool `cards_create`

Add a card (it gets the next #number). Lands in Requests / Sprinted unless `column` says otherwise. References (project, labels, assignees, item) are ids or names; unknown ones are refused with 400.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `column` | string |  | Board column: requests (Requests / Sprinted), doing (Doing), blocked (Blocked), uat (UAT), done (Done), must (Backlog: Must Have), nice (Backlog: Nice to Have). One of `requests`, `doing`, `blocked`, `uat`, `done`, `must`, `nice`. |
| `title` | string | yes |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `project` | string |  | Project id or name; "" for none. |
| `labels` | string[] |  |  |
| `points` | number | null |  |  |
| `due` | string |  | YYYY-MM-DD, or "" for none. |
| `assignees` | object[] |  |  |
| `assignees[].node` | string | yes | A person on a chart: node id or name. |
| `assignees[].role` | enum |  | One of `developer`, `tester`, `requester`. |
| `checklist` | object[] |  |  |
| `checklist[].id` | string |  |  |
| `checklist[].text` | string | yes |  |
| `checklist[].done` | boolean |  |  |
| `links` | object[] |  |  |
| `links[].id` | string |  |  |
| `links[].kind` | enum |  | One of `pr`, `commit`, `url`. |
| `links[].url` | string | yes |  |
| `item` | string |  | Timeline item id or title; "" for none. |
| `agents` | string[] |  | Delegate the card to these agents (replaces the list; [] for none). It joins each one's work queue (agents.work). |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `card` | object | yes |  |
| `card.id` | string | yes |  |
| `card.number` | integer | yes |  |
| `card.title` | string | yes |  |
| `card.description` | string |  |  |
| `card.column` | string | yes |  |
| `card.project` | string |  |  |
| `card.labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `card.points` | number | null |  |  |
| `card.due` | string |  |  |
| `card.assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.item` | string |  |  |
| `card.created` | string |  |  |
| `card.updated` | string |  |  |
| `card.moved` | string |  |  |
| `card.agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |

**Example: New card**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/cards" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Build sign-up form","project":"Lantern","labels":["High"],"points":3,"due":"2026-11-15","assignees":[{"node":"Cleo Park","role":"developer"}],"checklist":[{"text":"Email field"}],"item":"Public beta"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 51,
  "card": {
    "id": "k1",
    "number": 12,
    "title": "Build sign-up form",
    "description": "",
    "column": "requests",
    "project": "p1",
    "labels": [
      "l-high"
    ],
    "points": 3,
    "due": "2026-11-15",
    "assignees": [
      {
        "node": "cleo",
        "role": "developer"
      }
    ],
    "checklist": [
      {
        "id": "x1",
        "text": "Email field",
        "done": false
      }
    ],
    "links": [],
    "item": "i1",
    "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "moved": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "agents": [
      "a1"
    ]
  }
}
```

### `cards.update`

Update a DevOps card

`PATCH /api/v1/envs/{env}/cards/{card}` · scope `write` · MCP tool `cards_update`

Change a card's fields. Lists you send (labels, assignees, checklist, links) replace the old ones. The column only changes through cards.move, which applies the board's gates.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `card` | string | integer | yes | Card number or id. |
| `title` | string |  |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `project` | string |  | Project id or name; "" for none. |
| `labels` | string[] |  |  |
| `points` | number | null |  |  |
| `due` | string |  | YYYY-MM-DD, or "" for none. |
| `assignees` | object[] |  |  |
| `assignees[].node` | string | yes | A person on a chart: node id or name. |
| `assignees[].role` | enum |  | One of `developer`, `tester`, `requester`. |
| `checklist` | object[] |  |  |
| `checklist[].id` | string |  |  |
| `checklist[].text` | string | yes |  |
| `checklist[].done` | boolean |  |  |
| `links` | object[] |  |  |
| `links[].id` | string |  |  |
| `links[].kind` | enum |  | One of `pr`, `commit`, `url`. |
| `links[].url` | string | yes |  |
| `item` | string |  | Timeline item id or title; "" for none. |
| `agents` | string[] |  | Delegate the card to these agents (replaces the list; [] for none). It joins each one's work queue (agents.work). |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `card` | object | yes |  |
| `card.id` | string | yes |  |
| `card.number` | integer | yes |  |
| `card.title` | string | yes |  |
| `card.description` | string |  |  |
| `card.column` | string | yes |  |
| `card.project` | string |  |  |
| `card.labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `card.points` | number | null |  |  |
| `card.due` | string |  |  |
| `card.assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.item` | string |  |  |
| `card.created` | string |  |  |
| `card.updated` | string |  |  |
| `card.moved` | string |  |  |
| `card.agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |

**Example: Tick the checklist**

```sh
curl -sS -X PATCH "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/cards/12" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"checklist":[{"id":"x1","text":"Email field","done":true}]}'
```

### `cards.move`

Move a DevOps card

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/cards/{card}/move` · scope `write` · MCP tool `cards_move`

Move a card to a column (and position: `index` among that column's other cards; end if left out). The board's gates apply: into Done needs `confirm: true`, or `approve: true` from UAT (the Approve button); out of Done needs `confirm: true`; into Doing without a developer needs `developer` (a person, who is assigned) or `confirm: true` to leave it unassigned. A refused gate is 409 with code confirm_done, confirm_reopen or pick_developer.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `card` | string | integer | yes | Card number or id. |
| `column` | string | yes | Board column: requests (Requests / Sprinted), doing (Doing), blocked (Blocked), uat (UAT), done (Done), must (Backlog: Must Have), nice (Backlog: Nice to Have). One of `requests`, `doing`, `blocked`, `uat`, `done`, `must`, `nice`. |
| `index` | integer |  |  |
| `confirm` | boolean |  |  |
| `approve` | boolean |  |  |
| `developer` | string |  | Person node id or name. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `card` | object | yes |  |
| `card.id` | string | yes |  |
| `card.number` | integer | yes |  |
| `card.title` | string | yes |  |
| `card.description` | string |  |  |
| `card.column` | string | yes |  |
| `card.project` | string |  |  |
| `card.labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `card.points` | number | null |  |  |
| `card.due` | string |  |  |
| `card.assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.item` | string |  |  |
| `card.created` | string |  |  |
| `card.updated` | string |  |  |
| `card.moved` | string |  |  |
| `card.agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |

**Example: Approve from UAT**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/cards/12/move" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"column":"done","approve":true}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 53,
  "card": {
    "id": "k1",
    "number": 12,
    "title": "Build sign-up form",
    "description": "",
    "column": "done",
    "project": "p1",
    "labels": [
      "l-high"
    ],
    "points": 3,
    "due": "2026-11-15",
    "assignees": [
      {
        "node": "cleo",
        "role": "developer"
      }
    ],
    "checklist": [
      {
        "id": "x1",
        "text": "Email field",
        "done": false
      }
    ],
    "links": [],
    "item": "i1",
    "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "moved": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "agents": [
      "a1"
    ]
  }
}
```

**Example: Start work**

### `agents.work`

Get an agent's work queue

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/agents/{agent}/work` · scope `read` · MCP tool `agents_work`

What a runner needs to work as this agent: its `brief` and its queue, the open DevOps cards delegated to it (cards.update agents, or the card's Delegated to picker). Order: doing, requests, blocked, uat, must, nice (work in progress first; Blocked and UAT wait on others), then soonest due date, then #number. `columns` narrows the queue, e.g. ["doing","requests"] for cards it can act on now. Report back with cards.update (checklist, links) and cards.move.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `agent` | string | yes | Agent id or name. |
| `columns` | string[] |  | Only these columns (comma-separated in a query string). |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `agent` | object | yes |  |
| `agent.id` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.name` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.kind` | enum | yes | One of `agent`, `human`, `team`, `automation`. |
| `agent.title` | string |  |  |
| `agent.status` | enum | yes | One of `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `retired`. |
| `agent.live` | boolean | yes |  |
| `agent.reportsTo` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.supervisor` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.purpose` | string |  |  |
| `agent.instructions` | string |  |  |
| `agent.runtime` | string |  |  |
| `agent.models` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.model` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.auto` | boolean | yes |  |
| `agent.schedule` | string |  | When it runs: plain text or cron; "" for none. |
| `agent.job` | object |  |  |
| `agent.inputs` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.outputs` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.tools` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.projects` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.cards` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.items` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.created` | string |  |  |
| `agent.updated` | string |  |  |
| `agent.x` | number |  |  |
| `agent.y` | number |  |  |
| `brief` | string | yes |  |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].number` | integer | yes |  |
| `items[].title` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].description` | string |  |  |
| `items[].column` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].project` | string |  |  |
| `items[].labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `items[].points` | number | null |  |  |
| `items[].due` | string |  |  |
| `items[].assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].item` | string |  |  |
| `items[].created` | string |  |  |
| `items[].updated` | string |  |  |
| `items[].moved` | string |  |  |
| `items[].agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |

### `agents.create`

Create an AgentFlow agent

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/agents` · scope `write` · MCP tool `agents_create`

Add an agent to the AgentFlow org chart. References (reportsTo, supervisor, projects, cards, items) are ids or names; unknown ones are refused with 400, and a reporting loop with reports_loop.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `kind` | enum |  | agent (AI agent), human, team, or automation (a scripted job without AI that runs on its own schedule outside Flow: no models, never live). One of `agent`, `human`, `team`, `automation`. |
| `title` | string |  | Role, e.g. Research. |
| `status` | enum |  | One of `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `retired`. |
| `live` | boolean |  | The switch runners obey: false (the default) and runners leave the agent alone; true and the runner named in runtime works its queue. |
| `reportsTo` | string |  | The agent it reports to: id or name; "" for top level. |
| `supervisor` | string |  | A person on a chart who oversees it: node id or name; "" for none. |
| `purpose` | string |  |  |
| `instructions` | string |  | System prompt or runbook. |
| `runtime` | string |  | Where it runs: a runner name from runners.list, e.g. a home server. |
| `models` | string[] |  | Model ids the runner reported (runners.list), in order: the primary first, then fallbacks it tries when one fails (or, with auto, the pool it picks from). Also sets model to the first. Wins over model when both are sent. |
| `model` | string |  | One model id, e.g. claudeAgent:claude-sonnet-5-5: the same as sending models with just it ("" for none). Always reads back as the first of models. |
| `auto` | boolean |  | false (the default): the runner starts on the first of models and falls back in order. true: models is a pool and the runner picks one per card. |
| `schedule` | string |  | When it runs, in plain words or cron, e.g. "Weekdays 09:00" (a note carried in the brief for an AI agent; the reference runner does not start work from it); "" for none. |
| `job` | union |  | The runner job it was promoted from: {runner, id} (see runners.report jobs); null or "" for none. |
| `inputs` | string[] |  | What it takes in. |
| `outputs` | string[] |  | What it produces. |
| `tools` | string[] |  | What it may use. |
| `projects` | string[] |  |  |
| `cards` | string | integer[] |  |  |
| `items` | string[] |  |  |
| `x` | number |  | Canvas position (with y). Leave out to place it under its manager. |
| `y` | number |  |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `agent` | object | yes |  |
| `agent.id` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.name` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.kind` | enum | yes | One of `agent`, `human`, `team`, `automation`. |
| `agent.title` | string |  |  |
| `agent.status` | enum | yes | One of `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `retired`. |
| `agent.live` | boolean | yes |  |
| `agent.reportsTo` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.supervisor` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.purpose` | string |  |  |
| `agent.instructions` | string |  |  |
| `agent.runtime` | string |  |  |
| `agent.models` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.model` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.auto` | boolean | yes |  |
| `agent.schedule` | string |  | When it runs: plain text or cron; "" for none. |
| `agent.job` | object |  |  |
| `agent.inputs` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.outputs` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.tools` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.projects` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.cards` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.items` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.created` | string |  |  |
| `agent.updated` | string |  |  |
| `agent.x` | number |  |  |
| `agent.y` | number |  |  |

**Example: New research agent**

```sh
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Researcher","title":"Research","status":"active","reportsTo":"Chief of staff","supervisor":"Cleo Park","inputs":["A card that needs research"],"outputs":["Research notes on the card"],"cards":["#12"]}'
```

```json
  "agent": {
    "id": "a1",
    "name": "Researcher",
    "kind": "agent",
    "title": "Research",
    "status": "active",
    "live": false,
    "reportsTo": "a0",
    "supervisor": "cleo",
    "purpose": "Gathers context before work starts.",
    "instructions": "",
    "runtime": "T3",
    "models": [],
    "model": "",
    "auto": false,
    "schedule": "Weekdays 09:00",
    "inputs": [
      "A card that needs research"
    ],
    "outputs": [
      "Research notes on the card"
    ],
    "tools": [
      "Web search"
    ],
    "projects": [
      "p1"
    ],
    "cards": [
      "k1"
    ],
    "items": [
      "i1"
    ],
    "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z"
```

### `agents.update`

`PATCH /api/v1/envs/{env}/agents/{agent}` · scope `write` · MCP tool `agents_update`

### `agents.delete`

`DELETE /api/v1/envs/{env}/agents/{agent}` · scope `write` · MCP tool `agents_delete`

Remove an agent. Its direct reports move up to its manager, and workflow steps it ran become unassigned.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `agent` | string | yes | Agent id or name. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `deleted` | string | yes |  |

**Example: Remove the researcher**

```sh

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "rev": 58,
  "deleted": "a1"
}
```

### `runners.list`

List AgentFlow runners

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/runners` · scope `read` · MCP tool `runners_list`

Machines or services that run agents, with the models each one offers, as they last reported (runners.report). An agent's runtime names a runner and its models are some of that runner's model ids. Each model may say its provider (a display group) and billing (included or metered).

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].models` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].jobs` | object[] |  |  |
| `items[].timezone` | string |  |  |
| `items[].reported` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].jobsReported` | string |  |  |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |

**Example: Runners**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/runners" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
  "items": [
    {
      "name": "Home server",
      "models": [

          "billing": "included"

      "reported": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z"

  "rev": 42
```
